name: Ruth Cort
bio: Dr. Ruth Cort was a physician who went into exile in Czechoslovakia in July 1954 alongside her husband, Dr. Joseph Cort, when he fled the doctor draft and the threatened loss of his citizenship over alleged Communist ties. Denied a residence permit and facing removal herself, she shared the political exile that the McCarthy-era pressure forced on the family.
charges: Residence-permit denial and deportation pressure that drove her into exile with her husband, Dr. Joseph Cort.
convicted: No criminal conviction — went into exile in Czechoslovakia (1954).
sentence: Effective political exile from the United States.

name: Frank Hashmall
bio: Frank Hashmall was sentenced to five years for putting a false name and address on an automobile registration — a heavy penalty his defenders said reflected his being singled out and prosecuted as a 'Red' rather than the minor offense itself. His case was cited in the National Guardian as an example of political targeting dressed up as ordinary law enforcement.
charges: False name and address on an automobile registration — which his supporters charged was a pretext to punish him as a Communist.
